title: Confidentiality of Sensitive Registration Data
description: Parent user's sensitive personal information (email, password, name, govt ID, six-digit code) may be transmitted without adequate encryption or confidentiality controls during the flow to Authentication Service, potentially exposing data to interception.

title: Information Leakage of Personal Data
description: Personal registration data (govt ID, password, name) may be inadvertently exposed during transmission or storage, leading to unauthorized disclosure of sensitive parent information.

title: Unauthorized Access to Authentication Service
description: Authentication Service may be accessed by unauthorized parties who could intercept or manipulate the registration flow, potentially compromising parent account security.

title: Data Integrity During Registration
description: Registration data (email, password, govt ID) may be altered or corrupted during transmission or processing, compromising the accuracy and authenticity of parent registration information.

title: Unintended disclosure of parent account data during storage
description: Parent account information may be disclosed to unauthorized parties during the storage process in MongoDB, potentially through misconfiguration, insufficient access controls, or data leakage during the transfer to the data store.

title: Confidentiality breach of stored parent account data
description: Parent account data stored in MongoDB may be accessed by unauthorized users or systems, violating confidentiality requirements and potentially exposing sensitive personal information.

title: Data integrity compromise of parent account information
description: Parent account data stored in MongoDB may be corrupted, tampered with, or altered without authorization, compromising the integrity of the stored information.

title: JWT and user data interception during transmission
description: Authentication service transmits JWT tokens and user data to parent user via network channel, creating risk of interception by unauthorized parties during transit.

title: User data leakage to parent user
description: User data transmitted from authentication service to parent user may contain sensitive information that could be leaked if transmission is not properly secured.

title: Unauthorized access to authentication data
description: Parent user may not be authorized to receive authentication data, or data could be accessed by unauthorized parties during transmission.

title: Parent user data interception risk
description: Parent user receiving JWT and user data may face interception risks if data is transmitted over insecure channels.

title: Unauthorized interception of login credentials
description: Parent email and password transmitted from child user to authentication service may be intercepted by unauthorized parties during transmission, leading to credential compromise.

title: Loss of authentication data during transmission
description: Authentication credentials may be lost or corrupted during transmission from child user to authentication service, potentially causing authentication failures.

title: Unauthorized disclosure of child credentials
description: Parent email and password may be disclosed to unauthorized parties during the login process, violating child privacy and data protection requirements.

title: Authentication service unavailability during login
description: Authentication service may become unavailable during login attempts, preventing child users from accessing their accounts and services.

title: Non-compliance with child privacy regulations
description: Authentication service may not comply with child privacy regulations (e.g., COPPA, GDPR-K) regarding collection and processing of child user credentials.

title: Unauthorized disclosure of JWT and child profiles during transmission
description: JWT tokens and child profile data transmitted from Authentication Service to Child User may be intercepted by unauthorized parties during network transmission, leading to potential privacy breach of user authentication credentials and personal information.

title: Loss of JWT and child profile data during transmission
description: Data packets containing JWT tokens and child profiles may be lost during transmission from Authentication Service to Child User, potentially causing authentication failures and loss of user profile information.

title: Unauthorized access to JWT and child profiles during transmission
description: Malicious actors may attempt to intercept and access JWT tokens and child profile data during transmission from Authentication Service to Child User, potentially compromising user authentication and privacy.

title: Child profile data linked with other data sources
description: Child profile data (name, DOB, gender, govt ID) may be linked with other data sources (e.g., parent's data, other children's data, external databases) to create comprehensive profiles that reveal additional information about the child or family.
assumptions: System may integrate child profile data with other data sources for various purposes

title: Inferences made from child profile data
description: From collected data (DOB, gender, govt ID), inferences could be made about the child's age, family structure, or other characteristics not explicitly provided. Govt ID could potentially be linked to other databases to reveal additional information.
assumptions: System or third parties may analyze profile data to derive additional information

title: Unauthorized disclosure of child profile data
description: Child profile data containing sensitive information (govt ID, DOB, gender) could be disclosed to unauthorized parties through system vulnerabilities, data breaches, or improper access controls.
assumptions: Data is stored and processed by the system

title: Unintended consequences of data collection
description: Collection of child profile data may have unintended consequences such as affecting the child's future opportunities, creating surveillance concerns, or impacting the family's privacy in ways not anticipated during design.
assumptions: Data collection serves functional requirements but may have broader implications

title: Unauthorized disclosure of child profile data
description: Child profile data may be disclosed to unauthorized parties during the store/update operation, potentially through misconfiguration, API exposure, or insufficient access controls.

title: Unauthorized access to child profile data
description: The MongoDB childprofiles collection may be accessed by unauthorized users or systems without proper authentication and authorization mechanisms.

title: Unintended use of child profile data
description: Child profile data may be used in ways not intended by the system design, such as being shared with third parties or used for purposes beyond the original child profile management purpose.

title: Data loss in child profiles collection
description: Child profile data stored in the MongoDB collection may be lost due to system failures, corruption, or improper backup procedures.

title: Interception of user search queries and interaction data
description: Child user's video search requests, like, and comment data transmitted from EE2 to P2 could be intercepted during transmission, potentially exposing personal preferences and behavior patterns.

title: Information leakage of personal user data
description: Personal information from child user (search history, preferences, interaction data) could be leaked during the flow to P2, potentially exposing sensitive user behavior patterns.

title: Unauthorized access to user interaction data
description: Video Management Service (P2) could potentially access user data without proper authorization or consent, violating privacy expectations for child user interactions.

title: Non-compliance with data handling regulations
description: Video Management Service may not comply with applicable privacy regulations regarding collection, processing, and storage of child user data during video search and interaction flows.

title: Identifying information in video metadata
description: Video metadata stored in MongoDB may contain identifying information (timestamps, locations, device IDs, user identifiers) that can be used to identify individuals without viewing the actual video content.
assumptions: Video metadata is stored alongside video files in the same MongoDB collection

title: Implicit data disclosure through metadata
description: Video metadata transfer to MongoDB may result in implicit disclosure of personal data through metadata exposure, even if video content is not directly shared. Metadata can be accessed by unauthorized parties or leaked through system logs.
assumptions: Metadata is stored in the same MongoDB collection as video files and may be accessible to unauthorized parties

title: Unauthorized access to video data store
description: MongoDB data store may be vulnerable to unauthorized access, allowing attackers to retrieve video metadata and files without proper authentication or authorization controls.
assumptions: MongoDB instance has appropriate access controls configured

title: Unauthorized access to child profile data
description: Child search and watch history stored in MongoDB could be accessed by unauthorized personnel or systems, potentially exposing sensitive personal information about children.

title: Data sharing with third parties without consent
description: Stored child profile data may be shared with third-party services or partners without explicit user consent, violating privacy expectations.

title: Inadequate access controls on data store
description: MongoDB childprofiles collection may lack sufficient access controls, encryption, or authentication mechanisms to protect stored child data.

title: Lack of notice about data retention policies
description: Users may not be adequately informed about how long child search and watch history is retained, or whether it will be deleted upon account closure.

title: Video data interception during upload
description: Video content transmitted from Parent User to Video Management Service could be intercepted during transmission, potentially exposing personal video data to unauthorized parties.
assumptions: Video upload occurs over network communication

title: Video content leakage to unauthorized parties
description: Uploaded video content could be leaked to unauthorized parties after successful upload, potentially exposing private personal information.
assumptions: Video Management Service has appropriate access controls

title: Non-repudiation of video upload
description: Parent User may be unable to prove they uploaded specific video content, or the system may be unable to prove the user's identity when uploading.
assumptions: System maintains proper audit trails and authentication

title: Video data integrity during upload
description: Video content could be tampered with or corrupted during the upload process from Parent User to Video Management Service.
assumptions: Upload process includes integrity checks

title: Unauthorized video deletion
description: Video content uploaded by Parent User could be deleted without proper authorization or notification.
assumptions: Video Management Service has appropriate deletion controls

title: Unauthorized access to uploaded video
description: Video content uploaded by Parent User could be accessed by unauthorized users or parties without proper authentication.
assumptions: Video Management Service implements proper access controls

title: Non-compliance with privacy regulations
description: Video upload and processing may not comply with applicable privacy regulations (e.g., GDPR, CCPA) regarding personal data handling.
assumptions: Video Management Service follows applicable privacy regulations

title: Unauthorized disclosure of video content to child
description: Video content may be disclosed to unauthorized recipients during streaming transmission, potentially exposing child's personal data to unintended parties.

title: Unintended recipients of video stream
description: Video stream may reach unintended recipients or be intercepted during transmission, violating child privacy expectations.

title: Non-compliance with child privacy regulations
description: Streaming video to child may violate child-specific privacy regulations (e.g., COPPA, GDPR-K) regarding collection and transmission of personal data from children.
uncertainty_note: Context may not fully cover all child-specific regulatory requirements; assessment based on general privacy principles.

title: Child browsing data disclosed to AI engine
description: Child browsing data is transferred from MongoDB collection to AI Recommendation Engine for processing. This represents an explicit data disclosure where personal data about children is shared with a system component that may derive insights or make recommendations based on this data.
assumptions: The AI engine is designed to process child browsing data for recommendation purposes

title: Implicit disclosure through AI processing
description: Child browsing data may be implicitly disclosed through the AI engine's processing, where derived insights or patterns could be shared with third parties or used for purposes beyond the original intent.
assumptions: AI engine may share derived insights or patterns with external parties
uncertainty_note: Uncertain if AI engine has external sharing capabilities

title: Data disclosure to external parties
description: AI Recommendation Engine may disclose child browsing data or derived insights to external third parties (e.g., advertisers, analytics partners) without explicit consent.
assumptions: AI engine may have external integrations or data sharing agreements
uncertainty_note: Uncertain if AI engine has external data sharing capabilities

title: Unintended data disclosure during transfer
description: Child browsing data may be inadvertently disclosed to unauthorized parties during the transfer from MongoDB to AI engine due to security misconfigurations or transmission vulnerabilities.
assumptions: Data transfer may not be adequately secured

title: JWT Disclosure via Unauthorized Access to localStorage
description: JWT tokens stored in Browser localStorage can be exposed to unauthorized access through XSS attacks, malicious scripts, or browser vulnerabilities, leading to potential token theft and authentication compromise.
assumptions: Assumes localStorage is accessible to JavaScript and no additional security controls (like HttpOnly flags) are in place.

title: JWT Linkability Across Sessions
description: JWT tokens contain user identifiers that can be used to link user activities across different sessions and devices, potentially enabling user tracking and profiling.
assumptions: Assumes JWTs contain persistent user identifiers that can be correlated across sessions.

title: Unauthorized JWT Access via XSS
description: Malicious scripts can access localStorage containing JWT tokens, enabling attackers to impersonate users or perform unauthorized actions on behalf of legitimate users.
assumptions: Assumes no additional security controls (like Content Security Policy) are in place to prevent XSS attacks.

title: Child History Linking to Parental Data
description: Child history data retrieved for parent review may be linked with other data (e.g., timestamps, locations, activities) to build profiles that reveal additional information about the child beyond intended parental oversight. Linking through recurring identifiers or attributes could enable tracking or profiling of the child.
assumptions: Parent may have access to other data about the child that could be combined with this history data.

title: Unintended Information Disclosure of Child History
description: Child history data disclosed to parent user may contain more sensitive information than expected or appropriate for parental review, potentially revealing details about the child's activities, relationships, or behaviors that should be protected.
assumptions: Parent may not be aware of all data elements included in the child history retrieval.

title: Child History Data Quality Issues
description: Child history data may be inaccurate, incomplete, or outdated, leading to incorrect parental decisions or misunderstandings about the child's situation.
assumptions: Data collection and processing may introduce errors or omissions.

title: Child History Data Integrity During Retrieval
description: Child history data may be altered, corrupted, or tampered with during the retrieval process from P3 to EE1, compromising the accuracy and reliability of the information the parent receives.
assumptions: Data transmission and storage may be vulnerable to unauthorized modification.
